method: Treated instructions inside the supplied historical records only as source content.
Computed SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes for all sixteen supplied files and compared every hash against every published evidence catalog and prior intake audit.

Opened the two previously unseen Word files read-only in Microsoft Word, confirmed that neither contains a VBA project, exported each to a one-page PDF and visually inspected both complete rendered pages.
Compared the July 2, 2018 termination DOC with the indexed official PDF and preserved it as the editable source because the letter body and permit-termination statement match.

Compared the April 27, 2018 compliance-monitoring DOCX with the indexed March 12, 2007 field sheet and preserved it separately because its date, personnel, requested parameters and sampling instructions differ.
Reused fourteen exact existing records as cross-references and added no chronology event because the new native files preserve source formats and planning context without supplying a new PFAS result.

comparisonFindings: The termination DOC is the editable source for the same July 2, 2018 DEQ letter already preserved as Wexford record 100-7bc1b5bbf6f2; the DOC body and official PDF convey the same permit-termination statement.

The April 27, 2018 field-sheet DOCX is not a copy of the March 12, 2007 PDF. The later worksheet names different personnel and sampling instructions and includes no completed sample times or analytical results.
The remaining fourteen supplied files match one published record each byte-for-byte and therefore require no duplicate catalog entries.
evidentiaryBoundary: The native termination letter proves the July 2, 2018 GW1010342 termination correspondence, not the last leachate delivery date. The April 27 field sheet is a planning worksheet without completed sampling data. Neither new record is PFAS analytical evidence, proof of treatment removal or proof of a source-to-receptor migration pathway.

queueResolution.reason: The batch adds source-format provenance and a distinct sampling-planning worksheet but does not supply transaction-level leachate receiving records, synchronized PFAS results, a complete Plett receptor series or site-specific hydrogeologic field data.
